patch.summary: Reply.io migration guide: inventory → rehearse → freeze → validate integrations — grounded in researched limitations and catalogue peers.

blocks.body: Migrate to Reply.io by inventorying legacy sales-intelligence fields, mapping them to Reply.io objects, rehearsing a freeze window, and validating critical integrations before reopening writes.
bullets: Inventory → map → rehearse → cut over → reopen
Highest risk: Reply Data is a bundled convenience layer rather than a specialist database with published coverage figures
Success signal: contact management works for the pilot cohort

blocks.heading: Reply.io migration cutover playbook
blocks.body: Migrations fail from optimistic timelines — not from missing motivation.

scenarios.title: Field inventory
scenarios.body: Export legacy fields that power contact management, email sequences, lead scoring and mark must-map vs archive.

scenarios.title: Rehearsal load
scenarios.body: Run a non-prod load into Reply.io; measure match rates before the freeze.

scenarios.title: Production freeze
scenarios.body: Freeze legacy writes; cut over; validate primary integrations; then reopen.

steps.label: Migrate when Outbound SDR teams consolidating contact data and multichannel sequencing into one subscription outweigh migration cost
Delay if this limitation hits cutover: Reply Data is a bundled convenience layer rather than a specialist database with published coverage figures
If Reply.io mapping is poor, compare destination fit with Apollo.io before moving data twice

items.title: No freeze window
items.body: Dual-writing without a freeze creates irrevocable duplicates.

items.title: Integrations last
items.body: Wire systems of record in rehearsal — not on Monday morning after cutover.

items.title: Data risk 1
items.body: Reply Data is a bundled convenience layer rather than a specialist database with published coverage figures

items.title: Data risk 2
items.body: Jason AI SDR and Agency tiers are quote-gated, so the top of the plan ladder is not self-serve

items.title: Data risk 3
items.body: Mailbox warmup, LinkedIn accounts, and data credits create ongoing operational overhead per seat
